title: GLiTCH: GLiTCH induced Transitions for Secure Crypto-Hardware
problem: Power side-channel attacks exploit dynamic power profiles to infer cryptographic keys; conventional glitch reduction improves power efficiency but overlooks that strategic glitch manipulation can reduce correlation between power consumption and secret data.
motivation: Power side-channel leakage remains a critical threat to cryptographic hardware; exploiting glitch dynamics offers a novel defense complementary to traditional masking and randomization approaches.
method: The framework strategically adds or removes glitches (brief electrical pulses that occur unintentionally in circuits) by adjusting the size of logic gates—the small building blocks controlling signal flow in hardware. Adjusting gate sizes changes when electrical signals arrive at different points in the circuit, enabling the framework to control glitch behavior; this timing control is formulated as a geometric programming optimization problem (a mathematical approach that finds the best solution within constraints). Computer simulations validated the approach on three encryption algorithms—AES, CLEFIA, and SM4—ensuring they still work correctly and maintain good performance.
key_novelty: This is the first framework to strategically add or remove glitches (brief electrical pulses) to reduce power side-channel leakage—where attackers infer cryptographic keys by observing power consumption patterns—using geometric programming optimization.
contributions: Glitch manipulation via gate-sizing for arrival time control
Geometric programming formulation of glitch optimization
38.74% average area overhead across AES, CLEFIA, SM4
limitations: Trade-off analysis with other side-channel vectors (timing, EM) and resistance to adaptive attacks not discussed.
primary_theme: glitch manipulation for cryptographic power side-channel defense
